scientific_limitations: The observable is a differential log-survival slope, not a refitted b-value or finite-sample MLE.
The upper magnitude limit represents conditioning on the event lying below a fixed U, not random catalog maxima, censoring or data clipping.
Continuous mixing requires finite third rate moment; the two-slowest-rate asymptotic additionally assumes a finite mixture with separated positive rates.
The scope is analytic model comparison; no empirical seismic hazard or catalog priority is claimed.
title: A universal cutoff–heterogeneity transition for mixed Gutenberg–Richter slopes
